pharm: Relatively selective alpha-2 adrenergic receptor agonist that lowers intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous humor production and increasing uveoscleral outflow.
quick: One drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily, ~8 hours apart
No adequate human studies; use only if benefit justifies fetal risk
Not recommended (risk of CNS depression and apnea in nursing infants)
Intraocular pressure, ocular allergic/hyperemia reactions, alertness
summary: Brimonidine tartrate (ALPHAGAN P) 0.1% or 0.15% is an ophthalmic alpha-2 adrenergic agonist indicated to reduce elevated intraocular pressure in patients with open-angle glaucoma or ocular hypertension. It lowers IOP by reducing aqueous production and increasing uveoscleral outflow. It is contraindicated in neonates and infants under 2 years, and caution is advised in young children and with MAO inhibitors because of the risk of CNS depression and apnea.
indications: Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with open-angle glaucoma
Reduction of elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) in patients with ocular hypertension

dosage.d: One drop in the affected eye(s)
dosage.t: Three times daily, approximately 8 hours apart
dosage.n: May be used with other topical IOP-lowering products

dosage.t: Separate different products by at least 5 minutes

dosage.n: Somnolence and decreased alertness common, especially ages 2-6

admin: Instill one drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily, about 8 hours apart
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or surrounding structures (contamination risk)
Separate from other topical ophthalmic products by at least 5 minutes
Replace the cap after use; do not use if the solution changes color or becomes cloudy
moa: Brimonidine is a relatively selective alpha-2 adrenergic receptor agonist with a peak ocular hypotensive effect about two hours after dosing. Fluorophotometric studies suggest a dual mechanism: it lowers intraocular pressure by reducing aqueous humor production and increasing uveoscleral outflow.

absolute: Neonates and infants (pediatric patients younger than 2 years old)
Hypersensitivity to brimonidine or any component of the formulation
relative: Concomitant MAO inhibitor therapy (may increase systemic effects/hypotension)
Depression, cerebral or coronary insufficiency, Raynaud's phenomenon, orthostatic hypotension, or thromboangiitis obliterans
monitor: Ocular allergic reactions, conjunctival hyperemia, follicular conjunctivitis
Signs of CNS depression or apnea in young children

preg: There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. In animal studies brimonidine crossed the placenta into the fetal circulation to a limited extent, and caused miscarriage in rabbits at high oral doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit to the mother justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: It is not known whether brimonidine tartrate is excreted in human milk; in animal studies it is excreted into milk and crosses the blood-brain barrier. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, including central nervous system depression and apnea in nursing infants, ALPHAGAN P is not recommended for use during lactation.
renal: No dosage adjustment provided; systemic absorption from ophthalmic use is minimal.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment provided; brimonidine is extensively metabolized by the liver but systemic absorption from ophthalmic use is minimal.

major: MAO inhibitors: may interfere with brimonidine metabolism and increase systemic effects such as hypotension
moderate: CNS depressants (alcohol, barbiturates, opiates, sedatives, anesthetics): possible additive or potentiating effect
Antihypertensives and/or cardiac glycosides: brimonidine may further lower blood pressure
Tricyclic antidepressants: may blunt the IOP-lowering effect (affect amine metabolism/uptake)
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference noted.

serious: Severe cardiovascular effects in predisposed patients
CNS depression, apnea, bradycardia, hypotension in infants/young children
emergency: Apnea or severe CNS depression in a young child
Sudden vision loss from a contaminated solution / serious eye infection

monitoring: Degree of drowsiness/alertness, especially in children
Signs of vascular insufficiency in at-risk patients
counsel: Use exactly as directed: one drop three times daily, about 8 hours apart
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye or any surface to avoid contamination
If using more than one eye drop, wait at least 5 minutes between products
This medicine may cause fatigue or drowsiness; use caution with driving or hazardous activities
Keep out of reach of children; serious reactions including breathing problems can occur in young children
Seek care promptly for eye trauma, infection, or sudden vision change
pk: Ocular hypotensive effect begins within hours
Peak ocular hypotensive effect about 2 hours post-dose; plasma peak 0.5-2.5 hours
pearls: Contraindicated in neonates and infants under 2 years due to risk of apnea and CNS depression
Dual mechanism: reduces aqueous production and increases uveoscleral outflow
Caution with MAO inhibitors and CNS depressants; can cause systemic drowsiness
Somnolence is common in young children (up to 50-83% in ages 2-6)
Can be combined with other topical IOP-lowering drops, separated by at least 5 minutes
missed: Instill the missed dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and resume the regular schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up a missed dose.
overdose: Limited data on adult ingestion; the only reported reaction has been hypotension. In neonates, infants, and children, oral overdose or accidental ingestion can cause apnea, bradycardia, hypotension, hypothermia, hypotonia, lethargy, and CNS depression. Treatment is supportive and symptomatic; maintain a patent airway.
